request.spec:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Grace days are in, and periods now close on their own when the sheet's today moves past them. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **Setting:** grace days are a whole number, not dated. Blank means off. They're stored in a new nullable `grace_days` column on `sheet` (migration `V40__sheet_grace_days.sql`). They're set through a new `PUT /settings/grace-days` endpoint, and each save writes `SETTING_CHANGED ... key=grace-days value=<days>`. The settings view returns `graceDays` as a new field at the end.
- **Auto close:** `SheetService.setToday` saves the new today, then closes every open period whose to-date plus the grace days is before the new today, earliest to-date first. Only then does it write the rollup lines, all in one transaction. Each auto close uses the same code as a close by hand (I moved that code into a shared method in `PeriodService`), so the figures match. Its `PERIOD_CLOSED` line ends with `auto=yes`; a close by hand writes the same line as before, without it.
- **Screen:** the settings form has a `setting-grace-days` input (whole numbers only, with an error otherwise) and a `setting-grace-days-current` display.

**Choices to check**
- **No close permission check:** an auto close skips the check a close by hand makes. If whoever changes today isn't allowed to close periods, their periods still close. My reasoning was that changing today is the permitted action and the closing follows from it. If you'd rather it respect the permission, the check is easy to add.
- **Period list doesn't update by itself:** after a today change, the periods list keeps showing the old state until the sheet is reloaded. The tests reload anyway, so they pass either way.
- **Lookup when used:** `SheetService` gets `PeriodService` when it needs it rather than holding it directly. A direct reference would make a loop, because the period code depends on the claim code, which depends on the sheet code.
